_comment: The template for the scaling study's configs: copy it to configs/<study>.json, give it its run_name, data (student, sources, eval_sets, selection, selection_recipe) and schedule.epochs, and keep the rest unless the study decides otherwise. It is configs/viability.json (the first A100 run, which stays as it was run) with the changes its evaluation report recommends (section 9); every key not named here has viability.json's value and meaning (its _comment: the data, the selection recipe, the eval sets, the combined loss, the early stop). BATCH: batch.micro_audio_s 600 is the memory probe's first choice (memory_probe starts at batch.micro_audio_s, halves it on OOM down to memory.min_micro_audio_s, then turns on per-layer gradient checkpointing; the `memory_probe` event says what it chose). The first run paid ~0.137 s per micro-batch whatever its size (45 % of its 1.22 s step, at 4.07 micro-batches of 400 s per 1500 audio-s step); 600 s makes ~2.7 per step, an estimated ~1.04 s per step (~1,490 audio-s/s, +18 %) at ~29-30 GiB peak on the 40 GB A100 - extrapolated from that run, not measured. SCHEDULE: schedule.clock epochs with schedule.epochs 8: T = the optimizer steps of 8 full passes over the kept train rows (the `schedule` event), the warm-up at most 10 % of them, the WSD cooldown over their last 20 % counted in steps - no LR lost to eval pauses (the wall clock lost 16 % of the first run's cooldown LR integral to its evals) - and the last epoch's end is the final eval (no duplicate final eval, no tail of steps at LR ~0). schedule.train_hours and end_reserve_min do not apply on this clock, and the trainer does NOT shorten the run to the watchdog's deadline (fit_budget works on the wall clock only): size schedule.epochs so the run fits well inside vast/launch.py --max-hours (5.5 h from first boot): the steps per epoch (the `plan` event; 1,216 for the viability data at 1500 audio-s per step) x ~1.05-1.25 s, + ~4 min per complete eval, + ~10 min before the loop and ~5 min after it - 8 epochs of the viability data: ~9,700 steps, ~3-3.4 h of loop. EVALS: eval.full_every_epochs 2: the complete eval (teacher-forced and greedy on the complete eval sets, and the probe) at the end of every 2nd epoch, the mini eval every 500 steps in between as before (the first run spent 13 % of its loop on a complete eval every epoch). The early stop is viability.json's, so its patience of 3 evals now spans 6 epochs. THE VERDICT, PRE-REGISTERED (eval.verdict_version 2, kitsune.evaluate.verdict, whose docstring is the reference): the D32a tiers are unchanged - GO: student corpus CER <= 1.2x the teacher's on at least 2 of JSUT / CV8 / ReazonSpeech-test (the complete sets, the teacher on the same ids), truncation <= 0.5 % of the final outputs and the held-out minus probe KL gap not widening (its change <= +2 % of the mean held-out KL); PROMISING: <= 1.5x on at least 2 sets and CER still improving; NO-GO: fewer than 2 sets within 1.5x and CER not improving, or over-fitting (probe KL down by more than 1 % while held-out KL rises by more than 1 %); anything else INCONCLUSIVE. Version 2 fixes what the trends read (a trend = the least-squares slope across its window x the window's step span / the window's mean): (1) the eval records after step 0, in step order, lose every record that comes less than eval.verdict_min_epoch_gap (0.25) epoch after the previous kept one (the later one goes); (2) over-fitting and the KL gap: over the last max(3, ceil(0.2 n)) of those n records, cooldown included; (3) CER still improving: over the last max(3, ceil(0.2 m)) of the m of them whose eval followed a step at the peak LR (lr_phase stable: after the warm-up, before the cooldown - an early-stop cooldown counts), the mean over the 3 gate sets of student / teacher corpus CER changes by <= -1 %; on the complete sets' numbers when every record of that window has them (with this template every in-loop eval decodes the complete sets), else on the 500-per-set subset's; with fewer than 3 such records the trend is unknown ("trend: insufficient pre-cooldown evals"), so the run can be neither PROMISING nor that NO-GO; (4) reported next to the tiers, never gating: pre_cooldown_slope (that window's measure, its change and its slope per epoch) and cooldown_gain (the final eval against the last eval before the cooldown - the last lr_phase stable record of all the records after step 0, taken before the de-duplication in (1), so the eval nearest the cooldown's start even when (3) left it out: the measure before and after and each gate set's CER). With complete evals every 2 epochs and the cooldown over the last 20 % of 8 epochs (from epoch 6.4), the pre-cooldown evals are those of epochs 2, 4 and 6 - exactly the 3 v2 needs; fewer epochs or a larger cooldown_frac leave fewer (use full_every_epochs 1 or more epochs). On the first A100 run v2 gives the same INCONCLUSIVE as v1 did: -4.3 % over epochs 4-6 on the complete sets, its final eval (0.04 epoch after epoch 8's) de-duplicated, a cooldown gain of -10.7 % on the measure. REFERENCE MODEL: eval.reference stays null until configs/reference/parakeet-0.6b-ja.json holds Parakeet 0.6B ja's corpus CER on the complete gate sets - then {"name": "parakeet-tdt-0.6b-ja", "path": "configs/reference/parakeet-0.6b-ja.json"}; the file is {"name": ..., "scope": ..., "cer": {"eval_jsut": <fraction>, "eval_cv8": ..., "eval_reazon": ...}} (kitsune.evaluate.load_reference), read at setup, and the verdict reports the student's CER next to it per set and pooled, never gating. PROFILE: perf.profile_smoke true: smoke steps 22-41 under torch.profiler, runs/<run_id>/smoke/profile/summary.json (data wait, kernel time, launches and syncs per step and per micro-batch, top ops by self CUDA and self CPU time) and the first 2 steps' raw trace (kitsune.profiling); it does not change what the run trains - the evidence before any change for speed (torch.compile, the per-micro-batch syncs).
